industry.headline: UK Parliament research briefing updates status of under-16 social media ban proposal
industry.summary: UK government has formalized a June 2026 announcement of an under-16 social media ban (targeted early 2027) that goes further than Australia's model by also blocking livestreaming and stranger-contact for under-16s, plus new default midnight-6am curfews and anti-addictive-scroll defaults for 16-17 year olds. Directly relevant to the UK track where NOMO's CEO is influencing policy — a widening compliance window strengthens the case for third-party rewards tools as schools/platforms seek compliant alternatives.

industry.headline: New Mexico court orders Meta to pay $567M in landmark child-safety trial, on top of $375M jury penalty
industry.summary: A New Mexico court added a $567M remedial judgment against Meta (on top of March's $375M civil penalty) for knowingly harming children's mental health, with most funds earmarked for youth treatment services. This $942M combined judgment sets a concrete financial benchmark for addictive-design liability, reinforcing schools'/parents' appetite for court-validated alternatives like NOMO's rewards-for-offline-time model.

industry.headline: Global regulatory landscape update: Brazil, UK and US age-verification frameworks compared
industry.summary: Cross-market tracker confirms Brazil's Law 15.211/2025 is in force since March 2026, the UK's under-16 ban remains announcement-only (no bill yet), the UK's Online Safety Act has driven 69M+ age checks, and France just became the first EU country to legislate an under-15 ban (effective Sept 2026). Directly maps onto NOMO's three weighted regions (BR, UK, US/EU trend), giving concrete regulatory timelines for GTM messaging.

industry.headline: Social media addiction litigation tracker shows MDL growth and new state suits (Hawai'i) over youth harms
industry.summary: The federal Social Media Addiction MDL has grown to 3,137 pending lawsuits as of Aug 3, 2026, with Hawai'i becoming the latest of over a dozen states suing platforms over addictive design and weak age verification. Escalating litigation reinforces demand for alternative youth engagement models schools/districts can point to as a lower-risk complement to platform litigation.

industry.headline: Meta faces parallel trials in Tennessee and Oakland federal court as new teen-death suits pile up
industry.summary: Beyond the New Mexico ruling, Meta is on trial in Tennessee (AG suit over deliberate Instagram addictive design) and heading to a federal Oakland trial this month against four states from the 2023 multistate suit; separately, four families are suing Meta, TikTok, Snap and YouTube in Delaware over teen suicides. The volume and geographic spread of active trials signals litigation risk is now a sustained, multi-front reality — useful context for NOMO's US GTM messaging around proven demand for safer alternatives. (Consolidates duplicate coverage of the same Tennessee trial from other sources.)
